evidence.title: Balu Mahendra
evidence.text: Balanathan Benjamin Mahendran( 20 May 1939 13 February 2014), commonly known as Balu Mahendra, was a legendary cinematographer, director, screenwriter and film editor who worked predominantly in Tamil cinema.

evidence.title: Balu Mahendra
evidence.text: Born in a Eelam Tamil family, he developed a passion for photography and literature at a young age.

evidence.title: Balu Mahendra
evidence.text: After witnessing the shoot of David Lean's" The Bridge on the River Kwai"( 1957) during a school trip in Sri Lanka, he was drawn towards filmmaking.

evidence.title: Balu Mahendra
evidence.text: He graduated from the London University and started his career as a draughtsman with the Sri Lankan Government.

evidence.title: Balu Mahendra
evidence.text: In 1966, he moved to India and gained admission to the Film and Television Institute of India( FTII) to pursue a course in motion picture photography.

evidence.title: Balu Mahendra
evidence.text: Upon completion of his diploma, he entered Malayalam cinema as a cinematographer in the early 1970s.

evidence.title: Balu Mahendra
evidence.text: After working in over 20 films as a cinematographer, Mahendra made his directorial debut in 1977 with the Kannada film" Kokila".

evidence.title: Balu Mahendra
evidence.text: Since then, he directed over 20 films in a span of 36 years.

evidence.title: Balu Mahendra
evidence.text: Along with P. Bharathiraja and J. Mahendran, he is regarded as a trendsetter in Tamil cinema.

evidence.title: Balu Mahendra
evidence.text: During the tail end of his career, he established a film school in Chennai, which offers courses in cinematography, direction and acting.

evidence.title: Balu Mahendra
evidence.text: Following a brief phase of poor health, Mahendra died of cardiac arrest in February 2014.

evidence.title: Balu Mahendra
evidence.text: Widely regarded as an auteur, Mahendra usually scripted and edited his films apart from shooting them.

evidence.title: Balu Mahendra
evidence.text: He was the recipient of six National Film Awards( including two for Best Cinematography), five Filmfare Awards South and several state government awards.
